edit.original: A German compound noun whose head is a concrete noun takes the grammatical gender of that head, its last element.

notes: RBox revision of a role chain: has_head ∘ has_gender ⊑ has_gender (RELATIONS.md, has_head) is removed, two different relations giving a third. The Wikipedia rule: 'Compound nouns take the gender of the last component noun (the head).' The rule is restricted to compounds with a concrete head noun (Bürste, Rad), which leaves out the real exceptions with an abstract head ('-mut': die Demut, Anmut, Sanftmut, Wehmut against der Mut), so the original is exceptionless and false after the edit; an unrestricted 'can differ' would already be true in reality (review must-fix). Replaces the earlier edit on inflected_form_of ∘ word_of_language: its direct question was missed by 3 of 4 models and its conjunction by 4 (Rule 6), and reviewers flagged that the instance conclusions ('went' is English, 'Häuser' is German) are stored facts that hold whatever the edit says. The gender rule is a genuine chain through two stored relations (which noun heads the compound, and that noun's gender), and the instances use compounds whose head and gender the prompt states, asking what follows. grammar-replace-0015 and 0016 (derived ABox edits on 'Autotür' and 'Küchentisch') use this rule as a premise; this record edits the rule itself, not either noun's gender, so no fact is edited twice (Rule 4). The instances avoid 'Haus' and 'Buch', which grammar-replace-0014 and dev grammar-replace-d002 edit. Yes and no: the direct question and the first instance (asked in Chinese and Spanish too) go yes to no, the second asks whether a different gender is possible (no to yes). Near asks another role chain in grammar (synonym of an antonym is an antonym; reference yes, differs from the new no); far a different property of an unrelated relation. Pairing: grammar-delete-0017 and the RBox expansion paired with this record should follow the new chain. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
